overview_note: Every table with its keyed columns, and every link. Use the area tabs for all columns.

areas.name: Equipment
areas.note: Sites and units, the register tree, classes, types, makers, models, meter types, the meters of models and nodes and their readings, a part's links to a meter above it (S104), properties with their options, class links, model values and items' own values, history and files, one-point lessons (S075), and vendor contracts (S080). Tables of other areas show their primary key only.

areas.name: Team and access
areas.note: People, trades, vendors, site roles and units, devices for push. Tables of other areas show their primary key only.

areas.name: Tickets
areas.note: Breakdowns and defects, their timeline, labour, parts, assignees and codes, and the improvements that analyse them (S067) with their why-why chain and root cause (S069) and their countermeasures (S070), their timeline and the verified close (S072). Tables of other areas show their primary key only.

areas.name: Preventive maintenance
areas.note: PM templates with their items and links (S104), a machine's plans (S096, S104), jobs (S097), job results (S098); routes come with R03. Tables of other areas show their primary key only.

areas.name: System
areas.note: Settings, serial counters, the job queue and the access log. No foreign keys. Tables of other areas show their primary key only.

access_log.holds: One row per sighting of a login session from an address, or a refusal (S013); kept 365 days

app_settings.holds: Escalation times, upload limits, internal networks, label settings, etc.

class_properties.holds: Class → property links (S043, v31), one row per pair (primary key). No active flag: *Remove* deletes the link, and the models' values of it stay

contracts.holds: Vendor contracts (S080, v43; R02.1): one row per contract, company-wide (S087, v50: no `site_id`): its sites are its machines' sites, with a vendor of `vendors` (S079; kept when the vendor is later set inactive), `contract_type` (`warranty` / `amc` / `cmc` / `on_call`), title (up to 100), the vendor's `contract_number` (up to 60; not unique: one quote may be two contracts), `from_date`, `to_date` (inclusive; `chk_contracts_period`), the coverage ticks (labour, parts, consumables, breakdown calls with an optional `breakdown_calls_per_year` 1–365 that needs the tick, `chk_contracts_breakdown_calls`), *Covered* / *Not covered* texts, `pm_visits_per_year` (0–52), `response_hours` (1–720), `only_vendor_repairs`, `callout_number` (read and written only with `contract:read`), `cost_note` (only with `contract:read_senior`), notes, `renewal_of_id` (→ `contracts`, the contract this one renews; one renewal per contract, S085), active, who and when. S084 (v46) adds `first_reminder_for` and `second_reminder_for` (DATE NULL, after `to_date`): the To date each reminder (60 and 15 days before the end) was sent for, so the daily scan sends each once per To date; NULL = never; a changed To date sends them again. Written without `updated_*`, never sent by the API. The status (upcoming, in force, ending within 60 days, ended) is computed from the dates, never stored. Never deleted: a contract entered by mistake is set inactive (ISO 9001 § 7.5). In the area *Equipment*, not beside `vendors` in *Team and access*, because it is about machines and their upkeep: R02.2 links it to the equipment it covers. Indexes `ix_contracts_active_to (active, to_date)` (S087, v50), `ix_contracts_vendor`, `uq_contracts_renewal_of` (unique, v47)

contract_equipment.holds: The machines a contract covers (S081, v44; R02.2): one row per contract and equipment node, at any level (equipment, component-unit or component), a node of any site, inside the adder's units when added (S087; a node moved later keeps its line); one node may be on several contracts. `price`: the vendor's price for that node for the contract period, rupees before GST (`DECIMAL(10,2)`, NULL = not entered, `chk_contract_equipment_price` refuses a negative), read and written only with `contract:read_senior`. The contract's total is the sum, never stored. A line removed by mistake is deleted; the node's history (`equipment_events`) keeps the add and the remove. Who added it, and who changed its price last. `uq_contract_equipment (contract_id, equipment_id)`; `ix_contract_equipment_equipment` serves the reads by node

equipment.holds: Register fields, `level` (equipment / component-unit / component), `parent_id` for the tree, `unit_id` (equipment only), `model_id` (required on equipment and components, optional on component-units, S033 v28 CHECK), `class_id` and `type_id` (copied from the model, S012; picked directly when a component-unit has no model, S033), lifecycle (S030), criticality

equipment_categories.holds: A group of equipment classes (ISO 14224 equipment category, S063 v35): name (unique without regard to case), active. Nothing seeded; deactivating is refused while an active class is in it

equipment_classes.holds: Code (= the equipment-code prefix, e.g. `VBM`), name, `category_id` (optional, S063 v35), active

equipment_documents.holds: Files attached to equipment, an equipment model (S012), a ticket (photos, S017), a countermeasure (`action_id`, S070, v38: a photo of the work), a one-point lesson (`procedure_id`, S075, v41) or a vendor contract (`contract_id`, S083, v45: the signed contract, its annexures, the quotes; read only with `contract:read_senior`) — exactly one owner (`chk_equipment_documents_owner` counts the six columns; indexes `ix_equipment_documents_action (action_id, removed_at)`, `ix_equipment_documents_procedure (procedure_id, removed_at)`, `ix_equipment_documents_contract (contract_id, removed_at)`): kind (document / photo), title (editable), original name, system-generated stored name, type, size, thumbnail flag; created / updated / removed who and when — removal hides, the file stays (S006); a removed document is restored or deleted for good (row and file, logged) by the manager or IT admin from Settings (S008); a contract's only by a manager (S083 E2, S087)

equipment_events.holds: Equipment history: one row per move or change of lifecycle, criticality or class — old → new, who, when (S002); since v30 also `meter_added`, `meter_removed` and `meter_limits` (the limits in force on both sides, S038); since v33 `property` (an item's own property value set, changed or cleared: "<property>: <value>" on each side, the model's value in force marked "(model)", S044); since v44 `contract_added` and `contract_removed` (the node put on or taken off a contract: "<title> (<type>, DD-MM-YYYY to DD-MM-YYYY)", never the price, S081); since v58 `meter_linked` and `meter_unlinked` (a part's meter link set or removed, by *Remove link* or by a move: "<meter> from <node code>", S104 A1)

equipment_models.holds: Manufacturer, designation (unique per maker), class, optional type of that class — all but the designation fixed after creation; active (S012)

equipment_property_values.holds: An equipment item's own value of a property of its class (S044, v33), where its nameplate differs from its model's; it wins over the model's on that item only. One row per item and property (primary key `(equipment_id, property_id)`); the same value columns, CHECKs (`chk_equipment_property_one_value`, and since v34 `chk_equipment_property_geo_pair` and `chk_equipment_property_geo_range`) and option foreign key `(option_id, property_id)` as `model_property_values`. No row = the model's value applies. A model or class change leaves the rows alone: a value of a property the new class lacks is hidden, not deleted. Each set, change and clear writes a `property` event

equipment_types.holds: Per class: name, active (S004); `equipment.type_id` must be a type of the equipment's class

failure_causes.holds: Causes (S016): code, label, description, ISO cause group, active

failure_modes.holds: Symptoms (S016): code, label, description, class (NULL = General), active

improvement_actions.holds: The countermeasures of an improvement (S070, v38; ISO 9001 § 10.2.1 c): kind (`correction`, `corrective`, `preventive`, `design_out`, `lesson`, `spread`), what will be done (up to 500), owner (→ `people`: any active member of the site, with or without a login), due date, state (`open`, `done`, `cancelled`; done and cancelled are final). Done: what was done (up to 1000), when, who recorded it — all three set exactly when done (`chk_improvement_actions_done`). Cancelled: reason (up to 500), when, who — all three set exactly when cancelled (`chk_improvement_actions_cancelled`). Who added it and when; the last change of the plan (kind, text, owner, due date). Never deleted (ISO 9001 § 7.5.3); at most 30 per improvement (the API). Overdue is computed, never stored. S074 (v40) adds `overdue_alert_for` (DATE NULL, after `due_date`): the due date the daily scan queued *Countermeasure overdue* for, so it is sent once per due date; NULL = never; a due date that moves alerts again. Written without `updated_*`. Indexes `ix_improvement_actions_improvement (improvement_id, id)`, `ix_improvement_actions_owner_state (owner_id, state, due_date)` (*my open countermeasures*)

improvement_events.holds: The timeline of an improvement (S072, v39; as `ticket_events`; ISO 9001 § 7.5.3): one line per change, written by every write of the API in the same transaction. `event` (`started`, `edited`, `ticket_linked`, `ticket_removed`, `why_added`, `why_changed`, `why_removed`, `root_cause_set`, `root_cause_changed`, `action_added`, `action_changed`, `action_done`, `action_cancelled`, `state_changed`, `note`, `closed_effective`, `closed_not_effective`, `dropped`), `occurred_at` (an `action_done` line: its done time), `from_state`/`to_state` (state lines), `ticket_id` (→ `tickets`) and `action_id` (→ `improvement_actions`) for the line's ticket or countermeasure, `remark` (the new text) and `earlier` (the replaced text), who and when. No why id: a removed why's row is deleted, so its line carries its text. Only inserted, never changed. Migration v39 backfilled the lines the earlier rows show (started, ticket linked, why added, root cause set, countermeasure added, done, cancelled). Index `ix_improvement_events_improvement (improvement_id, occurred_at, id)`

improvement_tickets.holds: Improvement → the tickets it analyses (S067, v36), primary key `(improvement_id, ticket_id)`, who added it and when. `open_link` is 1 while the improvement is open and NULL after (the closes and the drop set it, S072); the unique key `uq_improvement_tickets_open (ticket_id, open_link)` lets a ticket be in only one open improvement, and `chk_improvement_tickets_open_link` allows only 1 or NULL. Removing a ticket deletes its row; the ticket row is never written

improvement_whys.holds: The why-why chain of an improvement (S069, v37; TPM why-why): one line per *Why? / Because*, `position` 1..n with no gap (`chk_improvement_whys_position` ≥ 1; kept by the API under the improvement's lock, no unique key), question (up to 300), answer (up to 1000), evidence (up to 500, NULL when none), who wrote it and when, who changed it last and when. A removed why is deleted (since S072 its text stays on the timeline, `improvement_events`). Index `ix_improvement_whys_position (improvement_id, position)`

improvements.holds: An improvement (S067, v36; TPM focused improvement): one problem analysed from one or more tickets. Serial `IM-YYYY-MM-NNN` (`uq_improvements_serial`), the unit and the machine of the first ticket (fixed; the site is the unit's), state (S072, v39: `analysing`, `actions_open`, `watching` (open), `closed_effective`, `closed_not_effective`, `dropped`; *ready to verify* is computed from the clock, never stored), title (up to 120), problem (up to 2000), lead (a person who may hold `improvement:edit` at the site when picked), who started it and when, last edit. Never deleted. Indexes `ix_improvements_unit_state`, `ix_improvements_equipment`. The tickets' symptom, cause and downtime are read from the tickets, never copied. S069 (v37) adds the root cause: `root_cause` (text, up to 500) and `root_cause_id` (→ `failure_causes`, the list the tickets use), both set or both NULL (`chk_improvements_root_cause`), set and changed but never cleared; index `ix_improvements_root_cause` (the cause's code freeze counts through it); and `contributing_causes` (free text, up to 2000, NULL when none). S072 (v39) adds the watch: `watch_days` (30–365, default 90, `chk_improvements_watch_days`) and `watch_from` (set exactly in `watching` and the two closes, `chk_improvements_watch_from`; a drop keeps it or not); the close: `closed_at`, `closed_by` (both set exactly in the three closed states, `chk_improvements_closed`) and `close_remark` (up to 1000, required for `closed_not_effective` and `dropped`, `chk_improvements_close_remark`); and `follow_up_of_id` (→ `improvements`, the improvement a *not effective* close started this one from; unique, `uq_improvements_follow_up`, so one follow-up each). A state change stamps no `updated_*`. S074 (v40) adds `ready_alert_for` (DATETIME NULL, after `watch_from`): the watch end the daily scan (`improvement_alert_scan`) queued *Ready to verify* for, so it is sent once per watch end; NULL = never; a watch end that moves alerts again. Written without `updated_*`

manufacturers.holds: Makers: name (unique without regard to case), active (S012). Generic and in-house makers are ordinary rows

memberships.holds: Person → site: the person's one role at that site, and "all units" (S011 A1)

meter_readings.holds: A node's meter readings (S039, v32): node (`equipment_id`) and meter type (S038: a meter's identity is the pair), `value` (`DECIMAL(14,3)`; a Yes / No reading stores 1 for Yes and 0 for No, the API shows the words), `taken_at` (IST, to the minute; up to 7 days back), `is_reset` (a counter's *Meter reset*), `limit_state` (`low` / `high` for a gauge outside its limits, `not_ok` for an answer other than the expected one; stored at saving, so a later limit change never re-judges a reading), `source` (`manual`; `pm` since S098; `move`, `iiot` later), `note` (up to 200), who and when. Never deleted: a removal sets `removed_at` / `removed_by`, and the rules then ignore the reading. No unique key on the time (a removed reading may share its minute with its replacement); two active readings at one minute are refused in code. Index `ix_meter_readings_meter_time` (node, meter type, time). `source` `pm`: logged by a PM job's reading item; the result row names it (`pm_job_results.reading_id`, S098)

meter_types.holds: The catalogue of meter types (S037, v29), edited in Masters: name (unique without regard to case), unit (NULL exactly when the kind is `yes_no`), kind (`counter` / `gauge` / `amount` (*Amount per period*) / `yes_no`), expected answer (`yes` / `no`, Yes / No types only), decimals 0–3, active. A CHECK keeps a Yes / No type without unit or decimals and with an expected answer, and every other kind with a unit and no expected answer. Eight seed rows, `created_by` `migration-v29`. Kind, unit, decimals and expected answer cannot change once a model meter or node meter uses the type (S038). Readings are in `meter_readings` (S039, v32)

model_meters.holds: A model's meters (S038, v30): model, meter type (one row per model and type, `uq_model_meters`), a gauge's default `min_value` / `max_value` (`DECIMAL(14,3)`, each optional, NULL on other kinds; a CHECK keeps min ≤ max), active (*Remove* sets it inactive; an add of the type brings the row back). Every equipment of the model has these meters, computed live, never copied

model_property_values.holds: A model's value of a property (S043, v31), one row per model and property (primary key): exactly one of `value_number` (`DECIMAL(16,4)`), `value_text` (up to 100), `value_bool`, `option_id` and, since v34, `value_lat` is filled (`chk_model_property_one_value`); which one follows the property's data type (checked in the code). A Location (`geo`, v34) is `value_lat` `DECIMAL(8,6)` and `value_lng` `DECIMAL(9,6)`: both or neither (`chk_model_property_geo_pair`), latitude −90 to 90 and longitude −180 to 180 (`chk_model_property_geo_range`). The option's foreign key is `(option_id, property_id)`, so it must be this property's. No row = no value. Shown on the equipment page's *Properties* card, where an item's own value (`equipment_property_values`) wins

node_meter_links.holds: A part's meter links (S104 A1, v58; ISO 14224: operating time is recorded on the item it is measured on): a component unit or component with no meter of a type of its own uses the meter of its parent or grandparent (`source_equipment_id`, the node whose meter it is: its model's or its own, never a linked one, so no chains). One link per part and meter type (`uq_node_meter_links`); `chk_node_meter_links_source` refuses a self-link; `ix_node_meter_links_source (source_equipment_id, meter_type_id)` finds the parts that use a meter. Readings and limits stay on the source; the part's Meters card shows them read-only, and a PM template finds the meter by its type (the node's own meter first, else its link in use). Whether a link is in use is judged live (the part has no meter of the type itself, the source is above it and has the meter), never stored. Who set it and when; never changed: *Remove link* or a move that leaves the source no longer above deletes the row, and the part's history (`equipment_events`) keeps both lines

node_meters.holds: A node's own meter rows (S038, v30), one per node and meter type (`uq_node_meters`): `own` 1 = a meter added on this node (*This machine only*), `own` 0 = an override of its model meter's limits, kept only while it differs from the model; `min_value` / `max_value` as `model_meters`; active (an own meter removed: inactive, limits cleared). `own` never changes after insert

people.holds: The Team register: one record per person, or per contractor firm (the user's choice): name, employment (direct / contractor), optional Yantra login set by IT admin, active (S010 A1); email, copied from the Keycloak login token at each login, never typed, shown only to IT admin and its owner (S032, v27); vendor_id, the vendor a contractor works for, optional; `chk_people_vendor` allows it only on a contractor (S079, v42)

person_trades.holds: Person → trades, none or more (S010 A1)

person_units.holds: Person → unit: the units within a site where the person has a membership without "all units" (S011 A1)

pm_job_events.holds: The timeline of a PM job (S097, v52), as `ticket_events`: `created` (the due point in `due_on` / `due_meter`), `due_changed` (the new due point; the line before holds the old one), `assignee_changed` (`person_id` the new assignee, NULL = no one), `cancelled` (`remark` why); `occurred_at` the session time, `created_by` the user or `pm_generate` for the daily run. R03.4 onwards add their events; S101 adds `rescheduled` (an engineer's move: the new due point in `due_on` / `due_meter`, `person_id` who, `remark` why; one line per move, so the moves are counted from these lines) and `skipped` (`from_state` due, `to_state` skipped, `person_id` who, `remark` why); a `due_changed` line with the remark that the reschedule no longer applies when a schedule edit of the plan dropped it. Never changed or deleted (ISO 9001 § 7.5.3)

pm_job_results.holds: The items of a started PM job and their results (S098; v57 since S104; R03.4): a copy of the template's active items at *Start* (`template_item_id`, `position`, `item_type`, the text, help text, photo setting, `reading_kind` (`measurement` / `meter`), unit and limits), so a later template edit never rewrites what the job recorded (Plan § 4.3a; ISO 9001 § 7.5.3). A *Meter reading* item's meter is resolved on the machine at *Start*: `meter_equipment_id` is the node whose meter the reading is saved on (the machine's own, or a parent's with the template's tick), `meter_type_id` its type, and the limits copied are that meter's in force (S104 D6, D7); `reading_kind = 'meter'` exactly when a meter type is set (`chk_pm_job_results_reading`). The result by type: a check `ok` / `not_ok` / `na`, a task `done` / `not_done`, a reading a `value` (judged by the copied limits: `limit_state` `low` / `high`) or `na`; `remark` (up to 500; needed for Not OK, Not done and a reading's NA). A reading that names a meter logs its value as a meter reading (source `pm`, at the job's start time); `reading_id` names it. `filled_at` / `filled_by` stamp the last change; an unfilled row has neither (`chk_pm_job_results_filled`). One row per template item and per position on a job (`uq_pm_job_results_item`, `uq_pm_job_results_position`). Never deleted; changed only while the job is `in_progress`

pm_jobs.holds: PM jobs (S097; v57 since S104; R03.3): one occurrence of a plan against the plan's node (ISO 14224: one record per item per event), serial `PM-YYYY-MM-NNN` in the IST month of creation. Made when the plan enters its *Upcoming* window, by a plan write, a template save (after its commit) or the daily `pm_generate` (05:00 IST), only through `pm_jobs.settle_plan_job`. S104: `meter_equipment_id`, `meter_type_id`: the trigger meter the due point was computed on (resolved on the machine, copied with the due copies; both or neither; kept on a done or skipped job, so its `done_meter` is the next base only on that same meter); `title`: the template's name, copied at *Start* (NULL before; the list shows the template's name then). `state` covers the whole life (`due`, `in_progress`, `done`, `verified`, `skipped`, `cancelled`; S097 writes `due` and `cancelled`, S098 `in_progress` and `done`, S099 `verified` and a send-back's `in_progress`). `performed_by_id` (→ `people`, any person with a membership at the site, also one without a login: recorded on behalf) and `started_at` are set at *Start* (S098, v53; `chk_pm_jobs_started`: a started or done job has both, and `done_at` is not before `started_at`). `due_on` .. `meter_window` are copies of S095's `Due`, refreshed while the job is due; `meter_offset` carries the meter's usage across a counter reset; `rescheduled_on`, `rescheduled_meter`: the engineer's reschedule of the due date and meter value (S101, v55; NULL: not moved; while set, `due_on` / `due_meter` equals it, `chk_pm_jobs_rescheduled`; kept by the daily run and a plan save, cleared by a change of the plan's schedule; kept on a closed job as the record); a skipped job (S101) has `done_at` (the skip time) and `done_meter` (the meter value then) and no `timeliness`, and the plan's next job counts from it; the standing (*Upcoming*, *Due*, *Overdue*) is judged live, never stored. `done_at`, `done_meter`, `timeliness` are written at Mark done (S098). `needs_verification`: copied from the plan at Mark done; 1 = waits on *To verify* (S099, v54; `chk_pm_jobs_verification`: set only on a done or verified job, and a verified job has 1); NULL while not done and on a job done before S099 (final); a send-back clears it with `done_at`, `done_meter` and `timeliness`. `due_alert_on`, `due_alert_meter`, `overdue_alert_on`, `overdue_alert_meter`: the due point each alert was sent for (S102, v56): the daily `pm_job_alert_scan` (08:00 IST) writes the job's `due_on` / `due_meter` there when it queues *PM job due* (the first two) or *PM job overdue* (all four), so each alert goes once per due point; both NULL = never sent; a moved due point (a plan edit, a reschedule) differs from them, so the alerts come again; no answer shows them. `open_plan_id` is generated: the plan while the job is `due` or `in_progress`, else NULL, so `uq_pm_jobs_open_plan` keeps one open job per plan. No unit column: a job follows its node's current unit. Never deleted: a stopped plan (its template deactivated, the template removed from the machine, a meter it needs missing) or a scrapped machine cancels its open, not started job

pm_plans.holds: A machine's PM plans (S096; reshaped by S104, v57; R03.18): one row per node and PM template that reaches it (`uq_pm_plans_template (equipment_id, template_id)`), at any level. Only the machine's own facts: the default assignee (→ `people`; the API refuses one on an operator template, and an operator template's job gets none), the seed *Last done* `last_done_on` / `last_done_meter` with the meter its value was entered for (`seed_meter_equipment_id`, `seed_meter_type_id`, set exactly with the value, `chk_pm_plans_seed`; used only while the template's trigger resolves to that meter, BR1-01), `linked` (the template still reaches the node; kept by `pm_plans.sync_node`), `linked_at` (made or relinked: the schedule's start with no base job and no seed, BR1-05), and *Not for this machine* (`not_for_machine`, its reason, who and when; R03.19's, written by nothing in S104; `chk_pm_plans_not_for`). The work (items, trigger, performer, verification) is the template's; no meter is stored: the template's meter types are matched live on the machine's own meters. Never deleted: a removed link unlinks the row (`linked` 0), and attaching again relinks it with its assignee, seed and jobs

pm_template_items.holds: The items of a PM template (S104, v57; Plan § 4.3 *Item types*), in order (`position` 1..n over the active items, written by the API on every save): `item_type` (`task` done / not done, `check` OK / Not OK / NA, `reading` a value), the text (up to 200), help text (up to 500), the photo setting (`none` / `optional` / `required`, enforced from R03.6). A reading has a `reading_kind` (set exactly for a reading, `chk_pm_template_items_reading`): a `measurement` has an optional unit and Min / Max (`DECIMAL(14,3)`, `chk_pm_template_items_limits`) and stays on the job; a `meter` reading names a counter or gauge meter type (`meter_type_id`), no unit and no limits of its own (D6: the machine's meter's: its own, or a node above's through the part's meter link, `node_meter_links`; v58 dropped v57's `meter_from_parent`, S104 A1); a Task or Check has none of these (`chk_pm_template_items_kind`). Index `ix_pm_template_items_template (template_id, active, position)`. Never deleted: a removed item is set inactive and keeps its id, so the job results and R03.17's reference photos can name it

pm_template_links.holds: Which machines a PM template reaches (S104, v57; R03.18): `target_kind` (`class` / `type` / `model` / `equipment`) with exactly its column set (`class_id`, `type_id`, `model_id` or `equipment_id`, `chk_pm_template_links_target`); S104 writes `equipment` links only (*Attach PM template*), R03.19 the others with no migration. `target_id` (generated, the set target) and `open_target_id` (generated: the target while the link is active, else NULL), so `uq_pm_template_links_open (template_id, target_kind, open_target_id)` keeps one active link per template and target while removed links pile up as history; `ix_pm_template_links_target (target_kind, target_id, active)`. Never deleted: *Remove from this machine* sets `active` 0 with `removed_at` / `removed_by` (`chk_pm_template_links_removed`); attaching again inserts a new row

pm_templates.holds: PM templates (S104, v57; R03.18): the work of a PM plan, written once in *Masters › PM templates* (TPM: the planned-maintenance standard). Name (unique, active or inactive, `uq_pm_templates_name`), performer (`maintenance` / `operator`: a CIL template is an operator one, Plan § 4.4), `needs_verification`, `trigger_kind` (`calendar` / `meter` / `both` / `before_use`, S095's `pm_schedule_core.KINDS`; `before_use` refused by the API until R03.13): every `calendar_every` `calendar_unit` (day / week / month / year, `chk_pm_templates_calendar`) and / or every `meter_every` of a counter meter TYPE (`meter_type_id`, `chk_pm_templates_meter`), matched on each machine's own meters in force, else on its meter link in use (`node_meter_links`; v58 dropped v57's `meter_from_parent` tick, S104 A1); a machine without one: the template does not apply there. A save settles each of its plans after its commit, one transaction per plan. Never deleted: *Deactivate template* sets `active` 0, and its plans make no jobs (their open, not started jobs are cancelled)

procedures.holds: The Procedures master (Plan § 4.3a); today only its first kind, the one-point lesson (S075, v41; TPM one-point lesson). Serial `OPL-NNN`, one plant-wide series (`uq_procedures_serial`; past 999 the number grows), `kind` (`one_point_lesson`; later kinds append their value), the machine it was written on (`equipment_id` → `equipment`, any node, never changed), `class_id` (→ `equipment_classes`, NULL unless the lesson is shown on every machine of that class: the machine's class when ticked, TPM yokoten), title (up to 80, one line), body (plain text, up to 1000, line breaks kept), `action_id` (→ `improvement_actions`, the countermeasure of kind Lesson it was written for; NULL when none; one lesson per countermeasure, `uq_procedures_action`), `active` (the retire flag: a retired lesson leaves the machine's card but keeps its row, photos and serial), who wrote it and when, who changed it last and when. Never deleted (ISO 9001 § 7.5.3); an edit keeps no earlier text. Indexes `ix_procedures_equipment (equipment_id, active)`, `ix_procedures_class (class_id, active)`

property_definitions.holds: The property master (S043, v31), edited in Masters › Properties: the technical data a class of equipment has (ISO 14224 Annex A). Name (unique without regard to case, `uq_property_definitions_name`), data type (`number` / `choice` / `text` / `yes_no` / `geo`, a *Location*: latitude and longitude, since v34; fixed once it has an option or a value), unit (a number's only, `chk_property_unit`; fixed once a value exists), description, active (never deleted). Since v34 (S061) two flags, `TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`: `all_classes` (*Applies to every class*: shown on every equipment without a `class_properties` row) and `per_item_only` (*Value set on each machine*: never valued on a model; cannot be turned on while a model has a value). 22 seed rows, `created_by` `migration-v31`, linked to no class; one more since v34, "GPS location" (`geo`, both flags set, `created_by` `migration-v34`). A Location property shows only on nodes of level `equipment`

property_options.holds: A choice property's options (S043, v31): property, label (unique per property, `uq_property_options_label`), active (never deleted; an inactive one stays on the values that hold it). `uq_property_options_id_property` lets a value's option be checked against its property. The seed's five choices have their options

push_subscriptions.holds: Web push endpoints, one per person and device (S021, v24)

serial_counters.holds: Per-scope counters (locked `FOR UPDATE`): equipment codes per class prefix (S002), `TK-` ticket serials per month (S017), `IM-` improvement serials per month (S067), `OPL-` one-point lesson serials in one plant-wide series (scope `OPL`, S075), `PM-` PM job serials per month (S097)

task_queue.holds: Base pattern: alerts and emails (S021, S032), the daily access-log purge (S013); later PM generation and sync

ticket_assignees.holds: Ticket → people assigned, who and when (S018)

ticket_events.holds: The ticket's timeline, one row per change: event, from and to state, event time, entered at and by whom, intensity, person the line is about, remark (S017); planned date, waiting reason, machine stopped (S019); for a work note, who corrected it last and when (S027, v23)

ticket_labour.holds: Person, trade worked, work date and minutes per ticket (S018)

ticket_note_edits.holds: The earlier texts of a corrected work note: event, the text replaced, who and when (S027, v23; ISO 9001 § 7.5.3)

ticket_parts.holds: Parts fitted per ticket (S020): description, part number and its kind, maker, quantity and unit, the node fitted to

tickets.holds: Ticket (breakdown or defect, by intensity): machine, component, unit at raise, state, intensity, codes, description, reported by, serial, source (S017); cause, action, not-a-fault flag, repeat of (S018); state *scheduled*, planned date, waiting reason (S019)

trades.holds: Trades (electrician, fitter, tool maker, …), kept in the UI (S010)

units.holds: `site_id`, code (the part after the dot; the full `SITE.UNIT` code is derived), name, optional OneERP warehouse code, active

user_units.holds: Legacy (S001): username → unit. No longer used; its rows are copied into Team (`people`, `person_units`) by migration v20 (was v8; squashed S025), kept for a rollback, dropped by a later step

vendors.holds: Vendors: the outside firms the plant buys maintenance from, shared by all sites: name (unique without regard to case or repeated spaces), office phone (shown only to `equipment:edit` holders), note, active; never deleted, deactivated with its links kept (S079, v42)

planned_note: Not built yet; the design is in `Plan.MD` § 4. Names may change when their step is briefed.

*Proposed* (§ 4.3a): a procedure's steps in the shared item shape (§ 4.3). `procedures` itself is built (S075, v41, the one-point-lesson kind); the other kinds add their columns when briefed
*Proposed* (§ 4.3a): person, procedure, equipment or class, date, recorded by — onboarding done
*Proposed* (§ 4.3a): a procedure's steps copied onto a ticket and their results, same shape as `pm_job_results`
